questions.q: In an Arkansas urban district, the maximum lawful speed on facilities other than the controlled-access highways described in section 27-51-201(b)(1) is
questions.explanation: Arkansas Code 27-51-201(c)(1) sets 30 miles per hour in any urban district, except when a special hazard requires a lower speed to comply with subsection (a).

questions.q: The 75 mph Arkansas maximum applies to a motor vehicle on a controlled-access highway that
options: Is inside any city, of any size
questions.explanation: Section 27-51-201(b)(1)(A) sets 75 mph only if the controlled-access highway is outside an urban area and has at least four lanes divided by a median strip. Subdivision (b)(2) requires the Arkansas Department of Transportation to erect signs giving notice of that limit. A commercial motor vehicle on that highway is limited to 70 mph under (b)(1)(B).

questions.q: On a controlled-access highway in an Arkansas urban area, the maximum stated in section 27-51-201(c)(3) is
questions.explanation: Section 27-51-201(c)(3) sets 65 miles per hour on a controlled-access highway in an urban area. That subsection covers facilities other than the outside-urban, median-divided highways in subdivision (b)(1).

questions.q: For a truck of one-and-one-half-ton capacity or more, in locations other than the controlled-access limits in section 27-51-201(b)(1), the maximum is
questions.explanation: Section 27-51-201(c)(2) sets 50 miles per hour for trucks of one-and-one-half-ton capacity or more in those other locations.

questions.q: Arkansas's 25 mph school rule applies when you are passing a school building or school zone
options: Whenever a school-zone sign is visible, at any hour
During school hours when children are outside
Only while a school bus is stopped
On interstate highways through a city
questions.explanation: Section 27-51-212(a) prohibits more than 25 mph when passing a school building or school zone during school hours when children are present and outside the building. Subsection (b) says the limit does not apply on freeways and interstate highways, or in a school zone protected by a steel fence that limits access to and egress from safety crossings.

questions.q: Arkansas makes it unlawful to operate or be in actual physical control of a motor vehicle if the alcohol concentration is
questions.explanation: Section 5-65-103(a)(2) uses an alcohol concentration of eight hundredths (0.08) or more in the person's breath or blood, based on the definition in section 5-65-204. Subsection (a)(1) separately covers operating while intoxicated.

questions.q: An underage person commits Arkansas's underage driving-under-the-influence offense with an alcohol concentration of
options: Any alcohol only on a boat
questions.explanation: Section 5-65-303(a) applies to an underage person who operates or is in actual physical control of a motor vehicle while under the influence, or while the alcohol concentration is two hundredths (0.02) but less than eight hundredths (0.08). The section also covers motorboats.

questions.q: Arkansas treats an alcohol-related offense under section 5-65-103 as
options: A crime that requires proof the driver intended to become intoxicated
An offense only if the concentration is over 0.15
A licensing rule with no criminal element
questions.explanation: Section 5-65-103(c) says an alcohol-related offense under that section is a strict liability offense. The underage offense in section 5-65-303(c) is also designated a strict liability offense.

questions.q: Under Arkansas's driver-services rule, accumulation of 14 or more points leads to
options: A notice of suspension or hearing
questions.explanation: 27 CAR 30-117 says 10 to 13 points produce a warning letter, and 14 or more points produce a notice of suspension or hearing. The notice must state the effective date and that failure to attend waives the hearing in favor of the suspension. The office may suspend no more than three months for 14 to 17 points, no more than six months for 18 to 23, and no more than one year for 24 or more.

questions.q: Arkansas assesses how many points for a driving-while-intoxicated conviction?
questions.explanation: 27 CAR 30-113(b)(1) assesses fourteen points for driving while intoxicated. The rule says those values are assessed for convictions within a thirty-six-month period measured from the date a person is scheduled for a hearing on the accumulation of moving-traffic convictions.

questions.q: Speeding 31 mph or more over the posted limit is assessed how many Arkansas points?
questions.explanation: 27 CAR 30-113 assigns eight points for speeding 31 mph or more over the posted limit, and five points for speeding 21 to 30 mph over the posted limit.

questions.q: An Arkansas learner's license is for ages 14 and 15 and allows driving
options: If accompanied by a licensed driver who is 21 or older
With any licensed family member of any age
questions.explanation: The Arkansas DFA learner's and intermediate license page says a learner's license is for ages 14-15 and authorizes operation if the licensee is accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older. Intermediate eligibility is contingent on no serious traffic violations or at-fault crashes during the previous 6 months.

provenance.manual: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration

questions.q: An Arkansas intermediate license is issued for ages
questions.explanation: DFA says the intermediate license is for ages 16-17 and authorizes a non-commercial motor vehicle. At 18, the person may apply for a regular license contingent on a clean driving record for the previous year.

provenance.manual: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration

questions.q: An Arkansas intermediate licensee shall not drive on public streets between 11:00 p.m. and 4:00 a.m. unless
options: With a licensed driver 21+, or for school, church, or work
A parent signs a yearly waiver that removes the hours entirely
questions.explanation: A driver with an intermediate license may not drive between 11:00 p.m. and 4:00 a.m. unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older, or driving to or from a school activity, church activity, job, or an emergency.

questions.q: Without a licensed driver age 21 or older in the front seat, an Arkansas intermediate licensee shall not carry more than
options: No passengers at all, including siblings
questions.explanation: Section 27-16-701 defines an unrelated minor passenger as someone under 21 who is not a sibling, stepsibling, or a child who resides in the same household. The intermediate licensee shall not carry more than one such passenger unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older in the front passenger seat.

questions.q: In Arkansas, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Arkansas issues a learner's permit for a car at 14 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Arkansas car permit: 14 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Arkansas, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Arkansas requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: Learner’s and Intermediate License – Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration

questions.q: In Arkansas, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Arkansas, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Learner’s and Intermediate License – Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration

questions.q: In Arkansas, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Arkansas drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Arkansas car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Arkansas car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Arkansas car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Arkansas car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Arkansas, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Arkansas, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Arkansas, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Arkansas, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Arkansas brings a suspension of 180 days.
questions.remember: Arkansas, first refusal: 180 days without a license.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Arkansas residential district?
questions.explanation: Arkansas sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Arkansas?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Arkansas can be posted up to 75 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Arkansas rural interstate: up to 75 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Arkansas's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Arkansas: only texting is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Arkansas?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Arkansas, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Arkansas left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

provenance.manual: VERIFIED CONSENT FOR A MINOR'S LICENSE

questions.q: How is Arkansas's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Arkansas seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Arkansas?
questions.explanation: Arkansas requires a car seat or booster until 6 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Arkansas: car or booster seat until 6 years.

questions.q: What is Arkansas's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Arkansas requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.
